question: Can deterministic constitutive-error refinement place 25-40 rows more effectively than both the rejected endpoint transform and naive log spacing?

algorithm.coordinate: uniform in log10(-h) over the existing generation interval per node
algorithm.initial_support: dry endpoint, wet K-branch endpoint and saturated endpoint handling unchanged
algorithm.score: max of normalized absolute theta interpolation error and normalized absolute log(K) interpolation error on dense analytical samples
algorithm.normalization: theta error divided by theta_s-theta_r; logK error divided by max(1, abs(log(Ksat)-log(Kdry)))
algorithm.refinement: insert the dense sample with largest score, deterministic lowest-index tie break, until requested support count
algorithm.interpolation_for_selection: piecewise linear only for support selection; final provider remains existing TSPACK

decision: Promote only if a sparse candidate materially reduces fidelity error at comparable runtime. Do not tune weights after observing candidate outcomes.
